subject: ventures/client-rebooking-predictor
professional: a customer-analytics / CLV data scientist who builds P(alive) and win-back models for service businesses (BG/NBD, Pareto/NBD practice), working with a salon owner's real booking exports; first checks: does the code compute what the method says, is the fitted rhythm biased by censoring, is the hold-out honest and calibrated, and does a real export (UK dates, vendor headers) parse correctly

evidence.correctness: Independent Python re-implementation from the README spec (stdlib statistics.NormalDist for the exact normal CDF, Gelman BDA3 normal-normal posterior written in precision form, golden-section MLE for pi, brute-force Mann-Whitney AUC) on the shipped sample: mu0 3.822397 = 3.822397, sigmaW 0.231950 = 0.231950, per-client pActive/pBack max diff 1.1e-6/1.5e-6 (the A&S erf approximation), segments 57/9/24/130 identical, back-test AUC 0.9440 = 0.9440, recency AUC 0.7141 = 0.7141, Brier 0.0927 vs base 0.2440 identical, lost value $45,701.63 identical. The engine is right. Inputs are not: a UK file 'ann,25/12/2025 / ann,07/01/2026' parses the second row as 2026-07-01 (each row guesses D/M vs M/D on its own); header 'Appointment Date,Amount Paid,Client' takes the amounts as client ids ('paid' matches /id/); 'Client,Service,Date,Price' skips every row ('service' matches the date regex first); '05.01.2026' becomes 1 May and '40,50' becomes 4050. These are silent on realistic exports, so correctness is capped at 2.
evidence.completeness: Loaded the served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs, then Chrome via Playwright): Load example renders 9 overdue / 24 due / 57 lost, verdict 'usable', back-test note, 33-contact plan, 9 overdue rows, no console errors, no horizontal scroll at 375px. Every README feature (segments, back-test with AUC/Brier vs base and recency, refusals at 30 clients / 40 gaps / 180 days, contact plan, template fill, both CSV exports, opt-out usage counting) is present and runs. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 32 pass, 0 fail, 0.18 s. Tests use known-truth simulations (lost precision >0.85, AUC > recency, pi near 1 when nobody leaves). Mutations with quality_mutate.py: 4 of 5 caught (overdue ratio 1.25->2.0, lost cut 0.2->0.1, pi likelihood return term zeroed, D/M swap); dropping k from the empirical-Bayes weight (calc.mjs:143) survived. The header-mapping and mixed-date cases above have no test.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (311 lines), index.html, usage.mjs, tests. Clean pure-function engine, no dependencies, escaped HTML output. Defects: header detection uses substring regexes that collide ('paid' contains 'id', 'service' and 'time' count as date columns) at calc.mjs:70-71; date order decided per row instead of per file (calc.mjs:35); client ids lowercased for matching and then reused as the display name in messages (calc.mjs:82, 305); fillTemplate passes the client name as a replacement string so '$&' expands; a dead no-op branch at calc.mjs:216 ('if (lastDay < asOf - 1) { }').
evidence.claims: Backed: nothing uploaded (no fetch/XHR, test page.test.mjs), disclaimer and 'not advice', 'Unverified: simulated businesses only', refusal thresholds, segment definitions, the back-test description; llms.txt served copy is clean. Not backed: the headline card says 'about $628 of one more visit each' (index.html:187) but $628 is the sum over the 9 overdue clients (recomputed: 627.82 total); the plan summary 'roughly $2,631 of one visit each' (index.html:169) has the same wording. README 'D/M/Y when unambiguous' is true per row but leads a UK user to expect their file is read day-first.
evidence.fitness: Job: a salon owner exports bookings and wants this week's call list. With an ISO or US-dated export and plain headers it works: a ranked list, a plan, messages, a CSV. A UK/EU owner gets silently wrong gaps; an export with a Service column before Date fails with 'found 0 clients'-type errors; messages read 'Hi ann lee' (lowercased). Usable for part of the intended users, a professional would hit these within the first hour.
evidence.domain: The method is a constant-pi cure mixture on lognormal gaps, close to the P(alive) idea in BG/NBD (Fader, Hardie and Lee 2005) with a hold-out against recency, which is the right practice. Departures: the gap model is fitted on completed gaps only, ignoring the open (right-censored) spell and the length bias of pooling gaps (fast clients contribute more), so the shop rhythm runs short. On data generated by the stated model itself (scratch calib.mjs): true median gap 35 d fitted 32.3-33.0; true median 120 d with sigma 0.5 fitted 94.5 and 95.1 (about 21% short), pi 0.85 fitted 0.785-0.805. One-visit clients borrow that short rhythm and are flagged due/overdue/lost early. Dropout is one shop-wide pi, not heterogeneous as in BG/NBD; no comparison against BG/NBD or Pareto/NBD.

defects.what: Day/month order is decided per row, so a UK/EU D/M/Y file is read day-first only on rows whose day exceeds 12 and month-first on the rest (07/01/2026 becomes 1 July), silently corrupting gaps; no warning. Decide the order once per file (any first field > 12 means D/M for the whole file) or ask.

Header detection uses substring regexes in column order: 'Amount Paid' matches the client regex via 'id', so amounts become client ids silently; 'Service' and 'Time' match the date regex, so 'Client,Service,Date,Price' reads zero rows. Prefer exact/word matches and the strongest match (e.g. 'date' over 'service').
Headline card and plan summary say '$628 of one more visit each' / '$2,631 of one visit each' but the number is the total across all listed clients.

Lognormal gaps fitted on completed gaps only, ignoring the right-censored open spell and pooling gaps so frequent clients dominate; on model-generated data a 120-day rhythm is fitted at about 95 days and pi 0.85 at about 0.79, so one- and two-visit clients are flagged due/overdue/lost early.
European formats misread: '05.01.2026' (always D.M.Y) parsed as 1 May; decimal-comma amounts in semicolon files ('40,50') parsed as 4050.
Client names are lowercased for matching and the lowercased form is used in messages ('Hi ann lee'); fillTemplate passes the name as a replacement string, so '$&' or '$1' in a name expands.
Dropping the visit count k from the empirical-Bayes shrinkage weight leaves every test green: no test checks that a ten-visit client leans on their own rhythm more than a two-visit client.

verdict: The statistical engine computes exactly what it documents: an independent Python re-implementation matches the fitted rhythm, every client's probabilities (to 1e-6), segments, back-test AUC and Brier, and value totals on the shipped sample, and the page runs end to end with no errors. It does not meet the bar because what a real owner feeds it is not read reliably: a UK D/M/Y export is silently mixed day-first and month-first row by row, a header containing 'Amount Paid' turns amounts into client ids, and a Service column before Date reads nothing. The headline '$628 of one more visit each' is a total, not per client. Methodologically the gap model ignores censoring, so slow-rhythm businesses get a rhythm about a fifth too short. Correctness 2, claims 2, verification 3; median 2.
